elements.title: Nayib Bukele (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele (pictured) has referred to himself as the "coolest dictator in the world"?

elements.title: Church of Santa Maria Maggiore (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that following its deconsecration, the Church of Santa Maria Maggiore in Venice and its grounds have been used as a stable, a tobacco warehouse, and a prison?

elements.title: Diana Edwards-Jones (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that television director Diana Edwards-Jones introduced earpieces to permit direct communication between a control room and newsreaders?

elements.title: St Francis of Assisi Church, Notting Hill (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that St Francis of Assisi Church, Notting Hill, contains a font designed by John Francis Bentley and in which he was later baptised?

elements.title: 1983 Spanish floods (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the 1983 Spanish floods were the most economically damaging in Spain until the 2024 Spanish floods?

elements.title: Castle Knob (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the medieval Castle Knob was the site of a Cold War nuclear monitoring station?

elements.title: Zhou Houkun (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Zhou Houkun wrote a thesis on the use of bamboo to reinforce concrete?

elements.title: Burrito Express (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Burrito Express began shipping out its burritos by mail because of demand from former customers who had moved away from California?

elements.title: Wu Tsai-fu (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that weightlifter Wu Tsai-fu drank six huge glasses of beer to help himself urinate for a drug test?
